extracted.intended_audience: Applicants, assignees, lessees, and counsel involved in ECIP transactions and cable landing license applications (telecom carriers, submarine cable operators, and regulatory compliance professionals).
extracted.subtask_description: Regulatory requirements and compliance criteria for participants in the FCC's Affordable Connectivity/ECIP program and for applicants/licensees of submarine cable landing licenses, including construction/operational benchmarks, holding periods, disqualifying conditions, routine license conditions, reporting, streamlining eligibility, and filing procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Construction period for ECIP assignees
rubrics_metrics.description: The construction period is the applicable construction deadline identified on the respective license(s), as extended by § 1.60005. If no such deadline remains for the license(s), the assignee must construct and operate, or provide signal coverage and offer service to, 100% of the Qualifying Geography no later than two (2) years after the consummation of the Commission approved application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies to assignees in Commission-approved Qualifying Transactions. Where interim/final performance benchmarks exist, this paragraph's requirements replace them (see paragraph (b)(3)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Replacement of interim/final performance benchmarks
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the assignee is subject to both an interim and final performance benchmark, the performance requirements in paragraph (b) shall replace the interim performance benchmark and the assignee shall not be subject to a final performance requirement. Where the assignee has only a remaining final performance requirement, the performance requirements in paragraph (b) shall replace the final benchmark.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicates ECIP-specific construction/operation benchmarks supplant prior interim/final benchmarks for the license(s) covered by the Qualifying Transaction.

rubrics_metrics.name: End-user device compatibility requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: All end user devices throughout the Qualifying Geography must be capable of operation on all spectrum bands associated with license(s) that contribute to the Qualifying Geography.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures devices in the Qualifying Geography support the spectrum bands of contributing licenses; applies to assignees of licenses in Qualifying Transactions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification of construction completion (Form 601)
rubrics_metrics.description: Notification of completion of construction must be provided to the Commission through the filing of FCC Form 601, no later than 15 days after the applicable construction deadline or the expiration of the two (2) year period in paragraph (b)(2) of this section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consistent with § 1.946(d). Timely Form 601 filing is required to evidence compliance with construction deadlines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Operational requirement for rural-focused transaction assignees (100% coverage for 3 years)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assignees in a Commission approved rural-focused transaction pursuant to § 1.60004 must construct and operate in, or provide signal coverage and offer service to, 100% of the Qualifying Geography identified in the Commission approved Qualifying Transaction for a period of at least three (3) consecutive years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operation/service must not fall below the level used to meet the construction requirement for the entire three-year period; must meet construction/operation by applicable deadlines or commence within two years after consummation where no deadline remains.

rubrics_metrics.name: Operation must not decline during three-year period
rubrics_metrics.description: Operation or service must not fall below that used to meet the construction requirement in paragraph (b) of this section for the entire three (3) year period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintains service quality/coverage level achieved at construction for the full operational period required of rural-focused assignees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing for rural-focused operational requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Assignees must construct and operate, or provide signal coverage and offer service, as required pursuant to paragraph (b) of this section, by the applicable construction deadline identified on the license(s), as extended by § 1.60005. Where no such deadline remains for the license(s), the three (3) year continuous operational requirement must commence no later than two (2) years after the consummation of the Commission approved application filed pursuant to § 1.60002.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies when the three-year operational clock must begin if no construction deadline remains.

rubrics_metrics.name: Construction and operational requirements for rural-focused leases (lessees)
rubrics_metrics.description: Lessees must construct and operate, or provide signal coverage and offer service to, 100% of the Qualifying Geography identified in the underlying Qualifying Transaction no later than two (2) years after grant of the underlying de facto transfer lease application or acceptance of the underlying spectrum manager lease application, and must maintain operation for at least three (3) consecutive years during any period within the initial minimum required five (5) year lease term.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies to lessees under rural-focused transaction prong; ties construction deadlines to lease grant/acceptance and requires a three-year continuous operational maintenance within the five-year lease.

rubrics_metrics.name: Initial operational requirement notification (ECIP)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assignees and/or lessees must file an initial operational notification with the Commission within 30 days of the commencement of operations that: (i) Provides the date operations began; (ii) Certifies that the operational requirement of 100% coverage of the Qualifying Geography for that assigned license or lease has been satisfied; and (iii) Provides technical data demonstrating such compliance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to demonstrate compliance at commencement of operations; must include technical evidence and an explicit certification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Final operational requirement notification (ECIP)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assignees and/or lessees must file a final operational notification with the Commission within 30 days of completion of the three consecutive year operational requirement that: (i) Certifies that the operational requirement of 100% coverage of the Qualifying Geography for three (3) consecutive years has been satisfied; (ii) Provides the date the three (3) year period was completed; and (iii) Provides technical data demonstrating the coverage provided during the three (3) year period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Required to evidence completion of the full operational commitment; includes certification, dates, and technical demonstration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Holding period for ECIP assignees (five years)
rubrics_metrics.description: An assignee of a license(s) granted in a Qualifying Transaction involving a partition and/or disaggregation or full assignment is required to hold any such license(s) for a period of at least five (5) years, commencing upon the consummation date of the Commission approved application filed pursuant to § 1.60002. During this holding period, except as provided in paragraph (g) of this section, the license(s) received through ECIP is not permitted to be further partitioned, disaggregated, assigned, or leased.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prevents immediate onward transfers of ECIP-obtained licenses; exceptions exist in paragraph (g) (e.g., pro forma transfers and specified interdiction system leases).

rubrics_metrics.name: Lease term and transfer restrictions for ECIP lessees
rubrics_metrics.description: Lease arrangements subject to the ECIP shall not be terminated by either lessor or lessee prior to the expiration of the five (5) year term required by § 1.60003(b)(3) or § 1.60004(b)(3), where applicable, and, except as provided in paragraph (g) of this section, may not be transferred or subleased to another party during the five (5) year term.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures minimum lease stability for ECIP-participating leases; paragraph (g) contains enumerated exceptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restrictions on subsequent transfers for rural-focused prong assignees
rubrics_metrics.description: Any license(s) resulting from a Qualifying Transaction under the rural-focused transaction prong pursuant to § 1.60004 may not be subsequently assigned (partition and/or disaggregation or full assignment), leased or transferred until: (i) The license(s) has been held by the assignee for at least five (5) years; and (ii) The construction and operational requirements pursuant to paragraphs (a) through (d) have been satisfied.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Both the five-year holding period and satisfaction of construction/operational requirements must be met before subsequent transfer.

rubrics_metrics.name: ECIP exceptions (pro forma and contraband interdiction)
rubrics_metrics.description: Requirements in paragraphs (a) through (e) do not apply to pro forma transfers pursuant to § 1.948(c)(1), and do not apply to any area of the Transaction Geography and/or Qualifying Geography which is covered by a lease or sublease entered into for the purpose of enabling a Contraband Interdiction System (as defined in § 1.9003).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identifies narrow exceptions to holding/operational and transfer prohibitions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Automatic termination penalty for ECIP noncompliance
rubrics_metrics.description: A license(s) resulting from a Qualifying Transaction in the ECIP shall be automatically terminated without specific Commission action or further notice if the assignee fails to comply with: (1) the five (5) year holding period; (2) the construction requirement or any remaining service-based performance requirement; or (3) the operational requirements, where applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Automatic termination supersedes any service-based penalty; applies specifically to ECIP licenses resulting from Qualifying Transactions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program bar from future ECIP participation
rubrics_metrics.description: A party participating in a Commission approved Qualifying Transaction in the ECIP shall be prohibited from future participation in the ECIP where it is found that it: (1) Violated the five (5) year holding period requirements; (2) Failed to meet the construction requirement or any remaining service-based performance requirement; (3) Failed to meet the operational requirements; or (4) Entered into a bad faith transaction in violation of § 1.60003(b)(4) or § 1.60004(b)(4).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enumerates grounds for disqualification from future ECIP benefits; includes premature lease termination, subleases, failure to meet buildout or operational commitments, and bad-faith transactions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect and scope of ECIP program bar
rubrics_metrics.description: A program bar commences upon notice via electronic mail finding a violation; barred party may continue to receive benefits conferred prior to the commencement of the bar. A program bar also applies to affiliates (as defined in § 1.60001); third-parties are affiliates if identified (or should have been) on initial application or identified (or should have been) in subsequent application. Transactions including a barred party are ineligible for ECIP benefits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Bar applies to affiliates and prospective participants where identification obligations were or should have been met; clarifies treatment of pre-existing benefits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cable landing license required prior to landing submarine cable
rubrics_metrics.description: A cable landing license must be obtained prior to landing a submarine cable that connects: (1) The continental United States with any foreign country; (2) Alaska, Hawaii, or the U.S. territories or possessions with (i) a foreign country, (ii) the continental United States, or (iii) each other; or (3) Points within the continental United States, Alaska, Hawaii, or a territory or possession in which the cable is laid in areas beyond U.S. territorial waters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies geographic scenarios triggering the licensing requirement under Subpart FF.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: foreign carrier (includes cable landing station owners/controllers)
rubrics_metrics.description: The term 'foreign carrier' is defined as in § 63.09 of this chapter except that it shall also include any entity that owns or controls a cable landing station in a foreign market.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expands foreign carrier definition to capture entities that own/control foreign cable landing stations for purposes of eligibility/streamlining and other rules in this subpart.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: third-party service provider
rubrics_metrics.description: A third-party service provider is an entity involved in providing, hosting, analyzing, repairing, and maintaining the equipment of a submarine cable system, including third-party owners and operators of network operations centers (NOCs).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines parties whose involvement in cable operations may be relevant to review and national-security considerations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: foreign adversary and foreign adversary country
rubrics_metrics.description: The term 'foreign adversary' is any foreign government or foreign non-government person determined by the Secretary of Commerce pursuant to Executive Order 13873. 'Foreign adversary country' refers to foreign governments identified as foreign adversaries in 15 CFR 791.4 and countries controlled by such foreign adversaries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to trigger presumptive disqualification rules and other national-security-related prohibitions and restrictions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: 'owned by, controlled by, or subject to the jurisdiction or direction of a foreign adversary'
rubrics_metrics.description: Applies to individuals/entities acting at the direction of a foreign adversary, citizens of foreign adversary countries who are not U.S. citizens or permanent residents, entities headquartered/incorporated in a foreign adversary country, or entities owned/controlled by a foreign adversary (including where any person in paragraphs (g)(1)-(3) possesses power via majority or dominant minority (10% or greater) voting/equity interest, controlling interest, board representation, proxy voting, special shares, contracts, or other arrangements).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets quantitative (10% dominant minority) and qualitative tests for foreign adversary ownership/control and thus for applying disqualifications/restrictions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: submarine cable system
rubrics_metrics.description: A cable system that carries bidirectional data and voice telecommunications traffic consisting of one or more submarine cable(s) laid beneath the water, and all associated components that support operation end-to-end, including segments up to terrestrial terminations at SLTEs and transponders converting optical to electrical signals and vice versa.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarifies scope of regulated infrastructure covered by cable landing licensing and conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Character presumptive disqualifying condition (20-year lookback)
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant will be presumed not to possess the requisite character qualifications to become a cable landing licensee if the applicant has within the last 20 years: (i) materially violated the Cable Landing License Act where the violation was not remediated with a consent decree/compliance plan, resulted in loss of Commission license, or was found intentional; (ii) committed national security-related violations of the Communications Act or Commission rules; (iii) made materially false statements or engaged in fraudulent conduct concerning national security or the Cable Landing License Act; (iv) been subject to adjudicated finding of making false statements or fraudulent conduct concerning national security before another U.S. Government agency; or (v) materially failed to comply with terms of a cable landing license including failure to comply with a mitigation agreement (with similar remediation/intentional/loss qualifiers).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establishes a broad character standard with detailed categories and consequences for applicants; the presumption can be rebutted (see paragraph (c)(3)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability and rebuttal of character presumption
rubrics_metrics.description: The presumptive disqualifying condition applies to initial applications filed after November 26, 2025 and to modification/assignment/renewal/extension applications filed after that date (with nuances based on when prior criteria existed). An applicant can overcome the adverse presumption only by establishing that the applicant has the requisite character; an applicant need not disclose pending investigations but must disclose violations preliminarily/finally determined by the Commission or adjudicated by another agency or court.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains when presumption applies and evidentiary approach for overcoming it; narrows disclosure obligations to adjudicated or Commission-determined violations.

rubrics_metrics.name: State Department coordination for cable landing licenses
rubrics_metrics.description: Cable landing licenses shall be granted or revoked by the Commission after obtaining the approval of the Secretary of State and such assistance from executive departments or establishments as the Commission deems necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reflects interagency requirement under section 5(a) of Executive Order 10530; State Department approval is required for grant/revocation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Foreign adversary presumptive disqualifying condition (ownership/control/covered list)
rubrics_metrics.description: The disqualifying condition will presumptively preclude grant of an application filed by any applicant: (i) that is owned by, controlled by, or subject to the jurisdiction/direction of a foreign adversary; (ii) that is identified on the Covered List maintained pursuant to the Secure Networks Act; and/or (iii) whose authorization/license/approval was denied or revoked on national security/law enforcement grounds, including current and future affiliates/subsidiaries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies to initial and certain later-filed applications after Nov 26, 2025; an applicant can only overcome the presumption through clear and convincing evidence that it does not fall within scope or that grant would not pose national security risks or that benefits substantially outweigh the risks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Foreign adversary cable landing presumptive disqualifying condition (landing in foreign adversary country)
rubrics_metrics.description: The disqualifying condition will presumptively preclude grant of an application filed by any applicant that seeks to land a new submarine cable in a foreign adversary country or to modify/renew/extend a license to add a new landing located in a foreign adversary country.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies to applications filed after Nov 26, 2025; rebuttal standard is clear and convincing evidence that applicant is not within scope or risk is mitigated/benefits outweigh risks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Routine license conditions: compliance with FCC rules, treaties, and Congressional action
rubrics_metrics.description: Grant of the cable landing license is subject to: (1) all rules and regulations of the FCC in this chapter; (2) any treaties or conventions relating to communications to which the U.S. is or may become a party; and (3) any action by the Commission or Congress rescinding/changing/modifying/amending any rights accruing to any person by grant of the license.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standard catch-all reserving applicability of other regulatory, treaty, or legislative changes to license rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Location conformity to Secretary of the Army plans
rubrics_metrics.description: The location of the cable system within U.S. territorial waters and shores shall be in conformity with plans approved by the Secretary of the Army. The cable shall be moved or shifted by the licensee at its expense upon request of the Secretary of the Army when necessary in the public interest, national defense, or for harbor maintenance/improvement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Limits placement/maintenance to Army-approved plans and gives Army authority to require relocation at licensee expense.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to comply with U.S. government location/concealment requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The licensee shall at all times comply with any requirements of U.S. government authorities regarding the location and concealment of the cable facilities, buildings, and apparatus for protecting and safeguarding the cables from injury or destruction by enemies of the United States.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: National security/safeguarding condition on cable operations and facility placement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restriction on handling telecommunications services without section 214 authorization
rubrics_metrics.description: The licensee, or any person or company controlling it, controlled by it, or under common control with it, does not enjoy and shall not acquire any right to handle telecommunications services to or from the United States unless such service is authorized by the Commission pursuant to section 214 of the Communications Act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Separates landing license rights from rights to provide cross-border telecom services absent separate authorization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on accepting special concessions from foreign carriers with market power
rubrics_metrics.description: The licensee shall be prohibited from agreeing to accept special concessions directly or indirectly from any foreign carrier, including any entity that owns or controls a foreign cable landing station, where the foreign carrier possesses sufficient market power on the foreign end of the route to affect competition adversely in the U.S. market, and from agreeing to accept special concessions in the future.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Protects against exclusive/anti-competitive arrangements with powerful foreign carriers that could disadvantage U.S. market competition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of special concession
rubrics_metrics.description: A special concession is an exclusive arrangement involving services, facilities, or functions on the foreign end of a U.S. international route that are necessary to land, connect, or operate submarine cables, where the arrangement is not offered to similarly situated U.S. submarine cable owners, IRU holders, or lessors. It includes arrangements for acquisition/resale/lease/transfer/use of capacity; access to collocation space; opportunity to provide or obtain backhaul; access to technical network information; and interconnection to the PSTN.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Helps identify prohibited preferential/exclusive arrangements with foreign carriers that would constitute a 'special concession.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Reliance on Commission's foreign carrier market-power list
rubrics_metrics.description: Licensees may rely on the Commission's list of foreign carriers that do not qualify for the presumption that they lack market power in particular foreign points for purposes of determining which foreign carriers are the subject of the special concessions prohibition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Directs applicants/licensees to an FCC-maintained list on the Office of International Affairs website for market power determinations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Environmental assessment and NEPA compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission reserves the right to require the licensee to file an environmental assessment should it determine that the landing of the cable at specific locations and construction of necessary cable landing stations may significantly affect the environment within the meaning of § 1.1307 implementing NEPA. The cable landing license is subject to modification under review of any environmental assessment or environmental impact statement required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: License grants may be conditioned or modified based on environmental review outcomes; see § 1.1307 and § 1.1306 notes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authority to impose common carrier or other regulation
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission reserves the right, pursuant to Cable Landing License Act, Executive Order 10530, and section 214 of the Communications Act, to impose common carrier regulation or other regulation consistent with the Cable Landing License Act on operations of the cable system if it finds the public interest requires.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commission retains regulatory flexibility to impose service obligations or other regulation if public interest warrants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain de jure and de facto control of U.S. portion
rubrics_metrics.description: The licensee, or in the case of multiple licensees, the licensees collectively, shall maintain de jure and de facto control of the U.S. portion of the cable system, including the cable landing stations in the United States, sufficient to comply with the requirements of the Commission's rules in this chapter and any specific conditions of the license.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures U.S. control (both legal and practical) of domestic cable infrastructure necessary for compliance and national security.

rubrics_metrics.name: License revocation/termination for noncompliance
rubrics_metrics.description: The cable landing license is revocable or subject to termination by the Commission after due notice and opportunity for hearing pursuant to section 2 of the Cable Landing License Act, or for failure to comply with the terms of the license or with the Commission's rules in this chapter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Due process-based sanction for violations of license terms or FCC rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: License term and expiration (25 years)
rubrics_metrics.description: The cable landing license shall expire twenty-five (25) years from the in-service date, unless renewed or extended upon proper application. Upon expiration, all rights granted under the license shall be terminated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standard license duration; licensee must timely seek renewal/extension to retain rights beyond 25 years.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commencement of service requirement and notice
rubrics_metrics.description: The licensee(s) must commence service provided under its license within three years following the grant of its license. The licensee must notify the Commission within thirty (30) days of the date the cable is placed into service. Failure to notify the Commission of commencement of service within three years following the grant shall result in automatic termination of the license after Commission receives approval from the State Department, unless the licensee submits a request for waiver showing good cause why it is unable to commence commercial service and why the license should not be terminated; commencement may be extended upon a showing of good cause.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires timely commencement and notification; provides waiver mechanism for good cause to avoid automatic termination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submarine cable outage reporting requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Licensees shall file submarine cable outage reports as required in part 4 of this chapter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mandates compliance with part 4 outage reporting rules separate from Subpart FF-specific filings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on using equipment/services on the Covered List
rubrics_metrics.description: A licensee whose application for a cable landing license is filed and granted after November 26, 2025, shall not use equipment or services identified on the Covered List that the Commission maintains pursuant to the Secure Networks Act on its submarine cable system under the license. A licensee whose modification application to add a new segment filed/granted after Nov 26, 2025 shall not use Covered List equipment/services on the new segment and new landing point. Licensees identified on the Covered List whose cable landing license was granted prior to Nov 26, 2025 are excepted from the paragraph (u)(1) prohibition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prohibits use of covered equipment/services on new licenses or new segments added after a cutoff date; preserves grandfathering for certain pre-existing licenses on the Covered List.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restriction on IRU/lease arrangements giving foreign adversary SLTE control
rubrics_metrics.description: The licensee shall not enter into a new or extension of an existing arrangement for Indefeasible Rights of Use (IRUs) or leases for capacity on submarine cable systems landing in the United States where such arrangement would give an entity owned/controlled by a foreign adversary the ability to install, own, or manage SLTE on a submarine cable landing in the United States, unless authorized by the Commission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Protects against foreign-adversary control of critical terminal equipment (SLTE); waiver possible only upon showing by clear and convincing evidence that the arrangement serves the public interest and presents no national security risks or benefits outweigh risks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quarterly reports for licensees affiliated with carriers with market power
rubrics_metrics.description: Any licensee that is, or is affiliated with, a carrier with market power in any of the cable's destination countries must file: (a) quarterly reports summarizing provisioning and maintenance of all network facilities and services procured from the licensee's affiliate in that destination market within 90 days from the end of each calendar quarter, containing types of facilities/services provided, volume/quantity provisioned and time interval between order and delivery, number of outages and intervals between fault report and restoration; and (b) quarterly, within 90 days from the end of each calendar quarter, a report of its active and idle 64 kbps or equivalent circuits by facility (terrestrial, satellite, submarine cable).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ongoing transparency requirement targeted at licensees with affiliation to carriers having market power in destination markets; specific content elements and timelines mandated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility for streamlining: general conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: Each applicant must demonstrate eligibility for streamlining by: (1) certifying it is not a foreign carrier and not affiliated with a foreign carrier in any of the cable's destination markets; (2) demonstrating pursuant to § 63.12(c)(1)(i)-(iii) that any such foreign carrier or affiliated foreign carrier lacks market power; or (3) certifying that the destination market where the applicant is, or has an affiliation with, a foreign carrier is a WTO Member and agreeing to accept and abide by the reporting requirements in § 1.70015. An application including an applicant that is, or is affiliated with, a carrier with market power in a cable's non-WTO Member destination country is not eligible for streamlining.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets out alternate paths to streamlining eligibility and a categorical ineligibility if affiliated with a carrier with market power in a non-WTO destination country.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certification of U.S. ownership for streamlining
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants for streamlining must certify that all individuals or entities that hold a ten percent or greater direct or indirect equity and/or voting interests, or a controlling interest, in the applicant are U.S. citizens or entities organized in the United States.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An ownership/nationality test as part of streamlining eligibility designed to ensure U.S. control of the applicant.

rubrics_metrics.name: CZMA consistency certification for construction/modification streamlining
rubrics_metrics.description: For a license to construct and operate a submarine cable system or to modify the construction of a previously approved submarine cable system, the applicant must certify that it is not required to submit a consistency certification to any state pursuant to section 1456(c)(3)(A) of the CZMA. Streamlining will be limited to those applications where all potentially affected states have waived, or are deemed to have waived, any section 1456(c)(3)(A) right to review within the thirty-day period prescribed by 15 CFR 930.54.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires CZMA clearance or state waiver for streamlining of construction/modify applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Streamlining eligibility for renewal/extension applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants for renewal or extension must include the information and certifications required for initial streamlining eligibility (paragraph (a)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Renewal/extension applicants are subject to the same streamlining certification requirements as initial applicants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Processing timelines for streamlined applications
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission will take action upon an application eligible for streamlined processing within forty-five (45) days after release of the public notice announcing the application as acceptable for filing and eligible for streamlined processing. If the Commission deems an application acceptable for filing but ineligible for streamlined processing due to national security/law enforcement/public interest concerns, or if applicant does not seek streamlining, the Commission will issue public notice indicating ineligibility. Within ninety (90) days of the public notice, the Commission will take action or provide public notice that an additional 90-day period is needed; successive 90-day periods may be extended.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets deadlines and extension mechanics for both streamlined and non-streamlined processing, including handling of applications raising extraordinary complexity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission to executive branch agencies at filing
rubrics_metrics.description: On the date of filing with the Commission, the applicant shall also send a complete copy of the application, or any major amendments or other material filings regarding the application, by electronic mail or postal mail to designated executive branch contacts (U.S. Department of State EB/CIP, NTIA Office of Chief Counsel, Defense Information Systems Agency), and to e-mail addresses identified on the FCC submarine cables webpage, and shall certify such service on a service list attached to the application or other filing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies required interagency service and certification obligations; Office of International Affairs may update contact information and agency list as needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Electronic filing requirement (ICFS)
rubrics_metrics.description: With the exception of submarine cable outage reports, and subject to the availability of electronic forms, all applications and notifications described in this subpart must be filed electronically through the International Communications Filing System (ICFS). A list of forms available for electronic filing can be found on the ICFS homepage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mandates electronic submission through ICFS for most filings in this subpart; outage reports remain an exception.

rubrics_metrics.name: Processing and service list amendment authority
rubrics_metrics.description: Authority is delegated to the Office of International Affairs to amend this rule and to amend the referenced website as necessary to update contact information and the list of agencies for filing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FCC staff may update administrative contact and filing lists without amending the core rule text.
